evidence.subject: 2026-11-03.ca.prop-1
evidence.claim: An annual public report on the bond's investments, using the existing state housing annual report (Health and Safety Code Section 50408). A yearly independent accountant review of CalVet's home loan finances. No target for homes built or cost per home.
evidence.excerpt: The administering entity shall publish in an annual report detailed information regarding the investments resulting from this bond pursuant to Section 50408 of the Health and Safety Code.
evidence.location: Health and Safety Code Section 54088, p. 103
evidence.explanation: Corrected after the audit: Section 54088 ties the annual report to Health and Safety Code 50408, which lists units, households and distribution. The old text understated the reporting. RESOLUTION. (1) Public reporting. The measure requires an annual published report (Section 54088) with 'detailed information regarding the investments' from the bond, 'pursuant to Section 50408'. Section 54088 itself names no metrics. It ties the report to existing Health and Safety Code 50408, which (as reproduced by HCD) requires the number of units assisted, households served and their incomes, and the distribution of units among areas of the state. For the Multifamily Housing Program, which gets $5.1 billion of the rental money, existing Section 50675.12 also requires that annual report to give the location of projects and units and the average cost per project and cost per unit. So the report must cover numbers and general locations of assisted homes, and per-unit cost for the main rental program. It is not a measure-specific list of every home. LAO says nothing about reporting. (2) Targets. Neither the statute nor LAO sets any target for homes built or for cost per home. LAO's 40,000 figures are 'up to' estimates. The only numeric unit rule is that at least 10 percent of assisted units in each funded development must be affordable to extremely low income households. That is an affordability mix, not a production target. (3) CalVet review. The independent accountant survey covers the financial condition of CalVet's Division of Farm and Home Purchases while the bonds are outstanding. It goes to CalVet, the Veterans Board, legislative committees and the finance committee. It is not described as public, and it is a review of the loan program's finances, not of the bond spending itself. (4) No State Auditor or other audit of the $10 billion housing money appears in the measure text. Our current text is accurate on targets but understates what the annual report must contain and slightly mislabels the CalVet review.
evidence.limitations: Sections 50408 and 50675.12 were read as reproduced in HCD's 2023-24 annual report, not from the codes directly (leginfo was not reachable through the tool). They could have been amended since. 'Administering entity' is not defined in the measure (reader found no definition), so which agency publishes is unclear. 50675.12 cost-per-unit reporting applies only to the Multifamily Housing Program share, not to the $2.1 billion preservation money, homeownership, farmworker, tribal, student or infrastructure money. Student housing money must meet Education Code 17201(i) and (o) reporting rules, which were not read. Re-checked Oct 23, 2026 (recheck_verdicts.py): the excerpt covers only part of the claim (name not in excerpt: CalVet's). Claim text updated on Oct 24, 2026 after correction P4; the excerpt is unchanged and backs the parts of the field it always backed.
